stacks.name: SharePoint web part (SPFx)
stacks.plain: A part you add to SharePoint pages or Microsoft Teams.

stacks.name: React web app
stacks.plain: A web app that runs in the browser, built with Vite.

stacks.name: Next.js website or app
stacks.plain: Pages built on the server: good for public sites and apps with sign-in.

stacks.name: SvelteKit web app
stacks.plain: A light, fast web app with very little code per page.

stacks.name: Vue web app
stacks.plain: A web app built with Vue and Vite.

stacks.name: SolidJS web app
stacks.plain: A very fast web app for screens with lots of live data.

stacks.name: Server / API (Node.js)
stacks.plain: A back-end service that other apps talk to.

stacks.name: ESP32 device (PlatformIO)
stacks.plain: Code that runs on a small ESP32 board, like the Box-3.

looks.name: Fluent UI
looks.plain: The Microsoft 365 look: matches SharePoint and Teams.

looks.name: Tailwind CSS
looks.plain: Style straight in the markup with ready-made classes.

looks.name: Plain CSS
looks.plain: Your own colours and spacing in ordinary CSS files, nothing extra to install.

looks.name: SCSS modules
looks.plain: CSS with variables and nesting, kept separate for each component.

looks.name: No screen
looks.plain: For servers and devices that don't have a user interface.

rules.name: Catch type mistakes early
rules.plain: TypeScript in strict mode, with every function and component input described.
rules.prompt: Use TypeScript in strict mode. Give every function, component prop and API response an explicit type; never use `any`.

rules.name: Tidy up after itself
rules.plain: Close connections, stop timers and remove listeners when something closes.
rules.prompt: Every timer, listener, subscription and connection must be cleaned up when its component or service closes.

rules.name: Always write whole files
rules.plain: No "…rest of code" gaps and no buttons that don't do anything yet.
rules.prompt: Always write complete files - never leave "...rest of code" gaps, placeholders or buttons that aren't wired up.

rules.name: No secrets in the code
rules.plain: Keys and passwords go in a .env file that never reaches GitHub.
rules.prompt: Keep keys, passwords and connection strings out of the code: read them from environment variables, list them in .env.example, and never commit .env.

rules.name: Tests from the start
rules.plain: Each feature comes with automated tests that run on every push.
rules.prompt: Write automated tests alongside each feature and keep `npm test` (or the stack's equivalent) passing; CI runs them on every push.

rules.name: British spelling and £
rules.plain: UK spelling everywhere, and money shown in pounds.
rules.prompt: Use British English spelling in all text, comments and docs, and format money in pounds sterling (£).

rules.name: Keep the project records up to date
rules.plain: Update the feature list, project map and test plan with every feature.
rules.prompt: Keep feature.json (one entry per feature), ProjectStructure.JSON (modules and how they connect) and test_plan.md (a test for each feature) up to date with every change.

rules.name: Read and write SharePoint data
rules.plain: Works with SharePoint lists and libraries through the page it sits on.
rules.prompt: Use the SharePoint page context and PnPjs (spfi with the SPFx behaviour) for all SharePoint list and library access; never hard-code site URLs.

rules.name: Live two-way updates
rules.plain: A live connection that reconnects by itself if it drops.
rules.prompt: Use a WebSocket for live two-way updates, with automatic reconnection and a heartbeat, and messages as typed JSON.

rules.name: Local database that upgrades itself safely
rules.plain: SQLite on the machine. When the data layout changes, the update finishes completely or not at all.
rules.prompt: Store data in SQLite (WAL mode, prepared statements). Apply schema changes on startup inside a transaction so an upgrade either completes or leaves the database untouched.

rules.name: Works for everyone
rules.plain: Keyboard-friendly, readable contrast and screen-reader labels.
rules.prompt: Meet WCAG 2.1 AA: everything usable by keyboard, visible focus, sufficient contrast and labels for screen readers.
